text:
ashley: heads-up — escalated ticket #42091 from Acme. They see a spike of 5xx during streaming responses. Customer says connections drop mid-stream and the request gets billed as a server error. link: https://redwood.support/t/42091 :warning:

ashley: quick summary:
- timeline: ~2024-06-20T15:24Z
- symptom: client abort during chunked response, gateway logs show write error then a 502/5xx recorded
- they attached a small curl repro they used from their infra

ben: can you paste one of the request IDs + the gateway trace? helps to correlate ingress vs runtime.

ashley: sure — request id r-0a9b3c, trace t-9f2e

ashley: gateway excerpt:
```
2024-06-20T15:24:12.341Z router[router-1] r-0a9b3c INFO route=/v1/stream client=10.1.x.x upstream=runtime-3 write_err=EPIPE: broken pipe downstream_closed=true status=502
2024-06-20T15:24:12.342Z runtime[model-gw-7] r-0a9b3c INFO kv_cache=hit sent_chunk=120 bytes
2024-06-20T15:24:12.342Z router[router-1] r-0a9b3c INFO end_request duration_ms=12 response_code=502 classification=upstream_write_failure
```

ashley: headers showed chunked transfer-encoding and no content-length. Customer says their client closes socket when they see partial output (they treat early stream as client abort).

liam: this looks like our counting logic in router: any upstream write failure is classified as 5xx. but if downstream_closed=true and the error is EPIPE, it's a client disconnect. we should avoid attributing those to server-side 5xx.

liam: repro I used locally:
```bash
# start a streaming request then kill the client socket immediately
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -o /dev/null &
sleep 0.2; pkill -f "curl -N"
```
results in router log "write_err=EPIPE" then a 502 recorded.

ben: agreed. two actions:
1) short-term: update metric/billing pipeline to ignore events where downstream_closed=true and write_err indicates client socket closed (EPIPE, ECONNRESET). treat as CLIENT_DISCONNECT for billing so customer's tokens aren't billed as 5xx.
2) medium-term: change router heuristics so these don't map to server 5xx in monitoring/alerts. add an explicit CLIENT_ABORT counter.

ben: can SRE add a filter to measurement pipeline to exclude these from the "server_errors" aggregation?

liam: yes — I can add a rule in ops-metrics to drop classification=upstream_write_failure when cause matches client-socket-closed. will also add a counter metric called router.client_abort.

devops-bot: deploy triggered: patch/metrics-filter-1737 -> staging (liam)

devops-bot: deploy succeeded: patch/metrics-filter-1737 -> staging (15:30:12 UTC) :white_check_mark:

ashley: updated customer with the workaround and asked for invoice hold while we confirm.

emily: (customer) thanks — volumes were peaking during a migration and our app closed idle listeners quickly. we'll re-run and share any repro traces. appreciate the quick follow-up. :pray:

ben: once liam's metric change lands to prod we'll reprocess that invoices batch to correct mislabelling.

liam: plan for prod rollout: patch metric rule -> canary (10%) -> full (1h). will post when canary flips.

devops-bot: canary started (10% traffic) 15:45:00 UTC

devops-bot: canary healthy, rolling to 100% 15:53:05 UTC

ben: closing loop — customer notified, billing team will re-eval disputed charges. follow-ups: add test to integration suite that simulates client abrupt close during chunked streaming so we don't regress.

ashley: thanks team. logging this thread into the ticket and tagging billing + evm for invoice reprocess. :thumbsup:
